method: Complete pinned source read, Git/SHA256 verification; compiled original NEON and previously reviewed portable sources with original headers, compared hash_many via ctypes.
findings: Little-endian ARM only; big-endian build explicitly rejected. Unaligned load/store helpers use byte intrinsics rather than aligned word access.
Four-input vector path transposes message and output lanes, applies seven rounds and per-lane counter. Remainder1..3 inputs calls portable compression, not separate NEON compression.
Counter increment occurs per input, not per block; flags_start applies first block and flags_end last. Callers must supply full64-byte blocks; partial final blocks handled by higher-level code.

540 comparisons all matched for input counts0..9,blocks1/2/16, counters0/2^32-2/2^64-4, both counter modes, three flag domains and one-byte-unaligned input buffers. Output buffers included16 zero guard bytes and entire buffers compared.
NEON and portable belong to same implementation family; parity is not an independent cryptographic oracle, all possible lengths or complete scanner correctness.

Source TODOs explicitly leave compress_neon/hash2_neon unimplemented. Single-input path cannot be assumed SIMD accelerated. Rotation microarchitecture-speed comments are upstream claims, not locally measured gains.

executed_control.scope: Original pinned NEON versus portable hash_many compiled and executed locally; shared implementation family, not independent cryptographic oracle or performance measurement.

limits: No sanitizer coverage, full upstream suite or throughput measurement.
